subject: people who didn't marry their high school sweetheart
tagline: Twitch for people who didn't marry their high school sweetheart
one_liner: Live-stream the timeline you picked. Chat watches the other one.
brand_voice_notes: Platform-operations deadpan. Almost discusses a private wound entirely in the language of creator monetization: retention, tiers, raids, rolling percentages. Nothing is ever named as sad. The product is described as working exactly as specified, because it is. Numbers are oddly precise. Sentences stop early.

hero.h1: Go live from the life you actually chose.
hero.sub: Almost is a streaming platform for the 41 million adults who did not marry the person from the yearbook. Dual-timeline broadcast, live chat verdicts, and subscriber emotes cut from your senior portrait.

features.title: Dual Timeline
features.blurb: Your camera on the left. On the right, a continuous reconstruction of the timeline where you stayed, assembled from one yearbook page, four saved voicemails, and their sister's public Facebook. Both feeds run at 1080p. Viewers pin whichever one they prefer.

features.title: The Verdict Meter
features.blurb: Every ninety seconds, chat votes on whether you made the right call. The rolling percentage sits under your handle permanently. It does not reset between streams. It does not reset between marriages.

features.title: Yearbook Emotes
features.blurb: We crop your senior portrait into forty-two reaction emotes. Subscribers deploy them during your worst moments. Tier three unlocks the one where you are wearing the rented tux.

pricing_tiers.name: Still Thinking About It
pricing_tiers.tagline: Entry tier. No commitment, which is thematically appropriate.
perks: One yearbook emote, selected by us

pricing_tiers.name: Drove Past The House
pricing_tiers.tagline: For the recurring viewer. Most people land here and stay.
perks: Monthly digest of their public posts, summarized

pricing_tiers.name: Full Reconstruction
pricing_tiers.tagline: Enterprise-grade. Invoiced quarterly. Nine seats minimum, for some reason.
perks: One raid on their actual channel, non-transferable
Printed year-end report, mailed to your current address

demo_screen_concept: A live channel page for an Almost broadcast. The player is split 50/50 into two timeline feeds with a pin control on each half, brass viewer-count and uptime plates beneath, and the Verdict Meter bar with right-call / wrong-call vote buttons that move the rolling percentage live. To the right, a scrolling chat panel with fake usernames, yearbook emotes, a working composer, and an emote picker. Left rail lists channels in your graduating class with live badges and a category filter. Follow and subscribe toggle in the channel header.

images.rationale: Whole budget on the two dual-timeline feeds, which are the product and the joke: same man, two lives, side by side. They do double duty as the hero's player card and the demo's player, so the hero slot is skipped rather than shot separately (a trophy-case chenille hero wants felt and brass, not a second photograph). Testimonial headshots skipped on purpose: the varsity direction turns those avatars into chenille monogram patches, which is more on-theme than three more portraits. 2 of 4 slots used.

Strictly no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no signage, no rendered UI screens, no phone or computer displays visible.
items.judge: accepted. Brass lamp lands on the primary hex, room falls off into the felt green, face reads unreadable rather than sad. No text, no UI, no AI-render tells.

design_direction.style: Varsity chenille and engraved brass, trophy-case dark mode. The page is staged as the inside of a lit high-school trophy case: a deep felt-green ground with chenille letter patches bolted to it and small engraved brass plates screwed on for anything numeric. Four motifs carry the whole page and nothing else is permitted. (1) The chenille patch: every card is a solid panel with a 7px felt border in the accent red, a 3px inner border in chenille cream, a 3px corner radius, and a 1px dashed cream stitch line inset 12px from the edge. Felt does not float, so every shadow is a single hard 3px down-right offset at 32 percent black with zero blur. (2) The engraved brass plate: all metadata, stats, dates, prices and eyebrow labels sit on small brass rectangles in #B8892B with a 1px lighter bevel on the top-left edge and a 1px darker bevel on the bottom-right, text set in dark inset brown, uppercase, letter-spaced 0.14em. (3) The felt ground: flat #12241C carrying a fine two-tone fiber speckle, never a gradient behind body text. (4) The case light: one warm top-down wash, a 180px cream-to-transparent gradient at 7 percent opacity pinned to the top edge of each major section, never a glow and never a blur. Explicitly absent: glass, backdrop blur, prismatic or holographic foil, terrazzo, risograph misregistration, leaded came, microfilm amber, galvanized panel, injection-moulded plastic, and the pharmaceutical leaflet grid.

fonts.body: 'Public Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Live-streaming creator platform landing page, video-first hero, written as athletic-department literature
design_direction.motion_vocab: 150 to 220ms ease-out, nothing longer. Chenille cards shift 2px down-right into their own hard shadow on hover instead of lifting, because felt is glued down. Brass plates flip their bevel to inset on press. The verdict meter animates its fill width only. One live-dot pulse on the whole page. Everything gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-bleed felt ground with the case-light wash pinned to the top edge. Left column: a brass LIVE plate, then an oversized Graduate h1 broken across two tight lines in chenille cream, then a 62ch sub in Public Sans at 18px, then a red chenille primary button and a ghost secondary. Right column: the dual-timeline player staged as a chenille-bordered panel split 50/50 by a 3px cream stitch rule, holding the two 4:5 timeline stills, with a brass viewer-count plate and the cream verdict bar directly beneath. Stacks to one column under 900px with the player first.
